title: Al bar e in trattoria
summary: Ordering politely at a bar or trattoria: vorrei, per me, mi porta…, and asking for the bill.

blocks.title: Ordinare con garbo
blocks.body: Four phrases get you through almost any bar or trattoria order: **vorrei** (I would like — softer than *voglio*, 'I want'), **per me** (for me — used when the table orders one by one: *'Per me, un caffè'*), **mi porta…?** (could you bring me…? — asking the waiter for something), and **il conto, per favore** (the bill, please, to close things out).
blocks.callout: *Voglio un caffè* isn't rude, exactly — but *vorrei* sounds like someone who's ordered coffee before.

items.en: Could you bring me the menu?

blocks.title: Le quattro frasi
blocks.body: Keep these in your pocket — they cover ordering, requesting, and paying.

rows: when the table orders one by one
to ask the waiter for something

blocks.prompt: You're at the table with friends and it's your turn to order. What do you say?
blocks.explain: *Per me…* is the classic one-by-one round order — 'for me, a coffee.' All three work, but this is the table-order convention.

pairs.note: Use *vorrei* with waiters, strangers, shopkeepers. Save *voglio* for close friends or urgency.

blocks.prompt: Type 'I would like a coffee, please.'
blocks.explain: *Vorrei un caffè, per favore.* — the safest, most universal order in Italy.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

lines.en: Good morning, I'd like a sandwich.
Could you also bring me some water?

blocks.scene: You and Marco grab lunch at a trattoria near his bookshop

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Vorrei il primo — la pasta al pomodoro.
lines.en: I'd like the first course — pasta with tomato sauce.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Buona scelta. Per me un panino, e un'acqua frizzante.
lines.en: Good choice. For me a sandwich, and a sparkling water.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Mi porta anche due caffè, alla fine?
lines.en: Could you also bring us two coffees, at the end?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Bravo, cominci a ordinare come un vero italiano.
lines.en: Nice, you're starting to order like a real Italian.
lines.spotlight: Notice 'mi porta' — a polite request aimed at the waiter, not at Marco.

blocks.prompt: Write your own order at a trattoria: what would you say to order a starter, ask for something extra, and ask for the bill?
